text: Region lives on customers, so I'll join order_items → orders → customers and products for price.

sql: SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'orders' ORDER BY ordinal_position

answer:
The South region generated the most revenue, at 1,201,250 (price × quantity summed over all order items, with no status filter). It is followed by West (1,173,750), North (1,162,500), and East (1,160,000).

South is also the top region if returned orders are excluded (the revenue figure is the same, since South has no returned orders in the data). Note that North drops out entirely when returned orders are excluded, so all of its 1,162,500 comes from returned orders.

sql:
SELECT c.region, SUM(p.price * oi.quantity) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY revenue DESC
SELECT column_name, data_type, is_nullable FROM information_schema.columns WHERE table_schema = 'public' AND table_name = 'products' ORDER BY ordinal_position
SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY status

SELECT c.region, SUM(p.price * oi.quantity) AS revenue
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY revenue DESC

SELECT c.region, SUM(p.price * oi.quantity) AS revenue
FROM order_items oi
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
JOIN orders o ON o.id = oi.order_id
JOIN customers c ON c.id = o.customer_id
WHERE o.status <> 'returned'
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY revenue DESC
SELECT status, COUNT(*) FROM orders GROUP BY status

answer:
The top region by total revenue is **south**, with 1,201,250.00 (sum of price × quantity over all order items, joining order items → products → orders → customers). Next are west (1,173,750), north (1,162,500), and east (1,160,000).

Excluding returned orders, south is still top at 1,201,250.00, but north drops out of the list entirely. Its revenue comes only from returned orders, so I'd expect the ranking to hold even though north's total is affected.

sql:
SELECT c.region, SUM(p.price * oi.quantity) AS revenue
FROM customers c
JOIN orders o ON o.customer_id = c.id
JOIN order_items oi ON oi.order_id = o.id
JOIN products p ON p.id = oi.product_id
WHERE o.status <> 'returned'
GROUP BY c.region
ORDER BY revenue DESC

answer: South is first. Revenue by region (price × quantity, all orders, any status): south 1,201,250; west 1,173,750; north 1,162,500; east 1,160,000. South ranks first either way. If returned orders are excluded, north drops out entirely (all its revenue comes from returned orders), leaving south 1,201,250, west 1,173,750, east 1,160,000.
